title: Cohomology over an affine base is the global sections of the higher direct images
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and assume that $S$ is affine [def-pc-scheme]. For every integer $q\geq0$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] there is an isomorphism of abelian groups
$$
e_{\mathcal F}:\;\Gamma\bigl(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)=H^0\bigl(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,\mathcal F),
$$
where $H^q(X,-)$ is the cohomology of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $R^qf_*$ the $q$-th higher direct image [pqf-def-cohomology]; these isomorphisms are natural in $\mathcal F$: for every morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, $e_{\mathcal G}\circ\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\varphi)=H^q(X,\varphi)\circ e_{\mathcal F}$. (The source states it for $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the separated case is the one stated here.)

source.place: Lemma 01XK (coherent-lemma-quasi-coherence-higher-direct-images-application), stated there for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated; proof by the Leray spectral sequence (Cohomology 01F2), quasi-coherence of R^qf_*F (01XJ (1)) and vanishing of higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on affines (01XB)

proof.text: *$f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.* The morphism $f$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. (Stacks states 01XK for $f$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; this step brings the separated case to it.)

source.place: Section 01KH, paragraph after Definition 01KK, using Lemma 01K7

proof.text: *The higher direct images are quasi-coherent.* Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Step 1), [lem-pc-ordinary-higher-image-quasi-coherent] (Stacks 01XJ (1)) says that $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module for every $q\geq0$. The source isQuasicoherent_higherDirectImage now specializes ordinaryHigherImage_isQuasicoherent definitionally.

source.place: Lemma 01XK, proof, second sentence: 'By Lemma 01XJ we see that the sheaves R^qf_*F are quasi-coherent'

proof.text: *The columns $p>0$ of the Leray spectral sequence vanish.* $S$ is affine [def-pc-scheme], i.e. isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ for a ring $A$; cohomology of modules is transported along an isomorphism of schemes (an isomorphism of ringed spaces identifies the categories of modules, their global section functors and hence their right derived functors [pqf-def-cohomology]), so [lem-pc-affine-vanishing] applies to $S$: every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module has vanishing $H^p(S,-)$ for $p>0$. With Step 2, $H^p(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F)=0$ for all $q\geq0$ and all $p>0$. (In the Leray spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=H^p(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,\mathcal F)$ these are the terms $E_2^{p,q}$, $p>0$.)

source.place: Lemma 01XK, proof, third sentence: 'By Lemma 01XB we see that E_2^{p,q}=0 when p>0'

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-module-cohomology-source-comparison] to identify the module-derived cohomology functor, after forgetting global scalars, with the source library H defined by Ext in abelian sheaves. This natural comparison transports affine vanishing to module cohomology on the base and, on X, supplies the final codomain identification.

*Degeneration gives the isomorphism.* By Step 3 the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections] (2) for the morphism $f:X\to S$, so the edge map $\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F}:H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F)$ of that node is an isomorphism of abelian groups for every $q\geq0$. Here $\Gamma(S,-)=H^0(S,-)$ on $\mathcal O_S$-modules: $H^0$ is the zeroth right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Gamma(S,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], computed from an injective resolution $\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ as $\ker(\Gamma(S,\mathcal J^0)\to\Gamma(S,\mathcal J^1))=\Gamma(S,\mathcal G)$ by left exactness. Put $e_{\mathcal F}=(\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F})^{-1}:\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F)=H^0(S,R^qf_*\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Lemma 01XK, proof, last sentences: 'Hence the spectral sequence degenerates at E_2 and we win. See also Cohomology, Lemma 01F4 (2) for the general principle.'

proof.text: *Naturality.* Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Steps 2-4 apply to $\mathcal F$ and to $\mathcal G$, so $\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F}$ and $\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal G}$ are isomorphisms, and [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections] (1) gives $\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\varphi)\circ\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F}=\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal G}\circ H^q(X,\varphi)$. Composing on the left with $e_{\mathcal G}=(\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal G})^{-1}$ and on the right with $e_{\mathcal F}=(\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F})^{-1}$ gives $e_{\mathcal G}\circ\Gamma(S,R^qf_*\varphi)=H^q(X,\varphi)\circ e_{\mathcal F}$, the asserted naturality.
